chapter: Cap, the city and its dances
title: Musicians he worked with: Hood, Eddie Johnson and Sidney Cates
summary: He recalls piano and banjo players such as Douglas Hood, Eddie Johnson and Sidney Cates.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Where was the guy from and what did he do?

He was a trumpet player. And he was from Norco or someplace out there. But he lived here too. How about Hood? Did you know him? Douglas Hood? Hood, he played banjo and he played piano. Yeah, I mean him. Did he work with animals? Yes, indeed. Because a lot of jobs I would get. And I called him to play piano with him. And then jobs he would get, he'd play piano and I would play banjo. I'd like to see Hood. I hadn't seen him in so long. I don't know whether he's still alive or what. And uh, Eddie Johnson, I played with him a lot of times. Which Eddie Johnson? Eddie Johnson. He died a couple of years back. What did he play? Saxophone. You talking about big head Eddie? The work at work? Right. Right. Right. Right. Yeah. That one. That one. Yeah. That one. Yeah. That one. That one. That one. Yeah. Yeah. And then I played with Sidney Cates. Oh, right. What was Cates playing? Cates was playing banjo. Oh, you had two banjos or banjo and get all? Yeah. Well, sometimes we played. Sometimes we played banjo and get all. Oh, I see. Yeah, Sidney Cates, I worked with him. Would that be a full ban or would that just be the two of them? No, it would be a full ban. I see. It would be a full ban. Because sometimes he didn't feel like going on the job and he'd play a while and he'd say, look at him, he'd say, I'm going to sleep off, I'm going home. Yeah. Because he was a carpentry too, you know. Right.
